_comment: SCHEMA for an RTO profile pack (assets/rto-profile.<rto>.json). This file is READ by scripts/Get-RtoProfile.ps1, not just documented by it: Assert-RtoProfile derives its required-key set, its closed palette role enum and its identity field list from here, so the validator and the specification cannot drift apart. Add a key to a profile and it is unvalidated until it is added here with a reason.
_whyThisExists: Everything a build would otherwise hard-code that is a property of the RTO rather than the unit lives in one versioned, validated file, assembled once per RTO and off the per-build critical path. One build ended up with ten build-local scripts hard-coding a single unit code, a single brand and that build's own counts, and three consecutive audits could only record the document-control block as 'not verifiable' because nothing declared what it was supposed to be.
_derivedNeverRestated: A profile pack POINTS AT its sources; it does not copy them. Identity strings and palette hexes are read from the branding profile, geometry and callouts from the guide profile, layouts and slot ordinals from the deck profile. A pack that restated a hex would be a second source of truth, free to drift from the map the brand swap actually applies - which is exactly how a crossover sweep came to print 'no crossover' over 766 live occurrences of another brand's fills.

keyReasons.schemaVersion: Which version of THIS file the pack was written against. A compiled contract that changes without a version bump is how two readers end up disagreeing silently.
keyReasons.rto: The brand key. Must match the branding profile's own 'brand' value, or the pack and the identity it claims are two different RTOs.
keyReasons.profileVersion: The pack's own version. The pack is cached across every unit this RTO ever builds, so a change to it has to be visible.
keyReasons.brandingFile: The branding profile this RTO's identity strings and palette are READ from. Named, never copied: the crossover sweep derives its forbidden set from the same files.
keyReasons.templates.guide: The approved, geometry-patched Learner Guide template. A brand with no approved template cannot be built - ask the RTO for one rather than generating it.
keyReasons.templates.deck: The approved deck template, same rule. The build clones an exemplar per layout and swaps its words.
keyReasons.guideProfile: Measured page geometry, heading colours, callout map and word floors for this RTO's guide.
keyReasons.deckLayouts: Layout names, slot ordinals, the numberSlot per layout, and the deck rules. Nothing else in the build may hold an ordinal.
keyReasons.noNotesReasons: One WRITTEN REASON for every entry on the deck profile's notesNotRequiredOn list. The list itself stays in the deck profile - one source of truth - and this is the audited register of why each exemption exists. An exemption with no reason is a shipped deck rule switched off where nobody reviewing the build would ever see it.
keyReasons.imageFraming.personNouns: The closed person-noun list the Stage 3b prompt lint matches at the head of a prompt's subject phrase. Closed and declared, because the lint is a string check and must never become a semantic judgement.
keyReasons.imageFraming.requiredNegatives: The negative constraints every prompt of a given subject class must carry. Set membership, per class.
keyReasons.lockedTerminology: Canonical terms, their forbidden near-synonyms and the required paired forms. Assessed terminology is never simplified, and the guide and the deck must call the same thing the same name.
keyReasons.documentControl: What a document-control block IS for this RTO, so an audit can verify it instead of recording it as not verifiable for the third round running.
keyReasons.carveOuts: Every declared exception to a rule, each with a written reason, surfaced to the audit as evidence. A carve-out nobody can see is a rule switched off quietly.

paletteRoles._comment: The CLOSED role enum. Palette resolution is a total function over it: a role with no match throws rather than falling through to a default, and a role that maps to itself throws, because a self-mapping role is an unresolved property name and never a legitimate no-op. The alias arrays exist because two differently shaped objects reach the swap - a branding file's own palette names the light fill 'lightFill', Set-HousePalette's return names it 'Fill' - and a single-name lookup fell through for that one role, mapped it to itself, and left 608 foreign light fills in a guide and 158 in a deck that both passed a crossover sweep.

identityFields._comment: Every identity string a delivered artefact can carry, and therefore every string another brand's profile makes forbidden in this one. Required fields must be present in the branding profile for the pack to validate; the rest are swept when present.

authorityClasses._comment: The closed enum every registry figure is classed against in the provenance audit. A figure that fits none of the four is fabricated, however reasonable it looks.
authorityClasses.P: the assessment pack - upstream, and it wins
authorityClasses.L: named legislation, a standard or a code, cited
authorityClasses.V: the scenario venue's own documented procedure, and said so on the page
